title: MacFlayer Config, schema version 1
description: PROTOTYPE. A Config lists what a Machine should have. Every object is closed: a field this schema doesn't name is an error, which is what keeps shell commands, trust grants, removal flags and includes out. Once published, this version is frozen: tightening a rule later would break files that are valid today, so it needs a new schemaVersion. Rules that can change between releases aren't here. Whether an ID exists, whether a value suits its Item, secret checks and link safety run after this schema passes, entry by entry. Patterns are plain ECMA-262 with no lookaround, so Rust's regex crate compiles them.

$schema.description: Editor hint for completion and checking. Any string, so a repo rename or a local path doesn't refuse the file. The app never fetches it or shows it.

schemaVersion.description: The format version. An app that doesn't know this number refuses the file and changes nothing.

name.description: Shown in the app, as data from the file's author. There is no description field: prose belongs in the Config Repo's README.

items.description: Catalog Items to install or complete: apps, CLIs and Machine-value Items such as git-identity. Settings go in `settings`.

packages.description: Homebrew packages the Catalog doesn't cover. Names only: no options, versions or trust.

settings.description: Setting Item ID to desired value. Leaving an ID out means the app doesn't manage that setting.

dotfiles.description: The Dotfiles Repo. A Dotfiles Repo is code, so this whole block needs approval on the Machine, tied to the repo and a commit. The clone location and the approval are Machine-local, so neither is here.

repo.description: owner/repo on GitHub, or an https URL with no credentials in it. A port is allowed.

links.description: Link location on the Machine to path inside the Dotfiles Repo, one link per line. The app also refuses overlapping locations and protected folders, per link.

installScript.description: Path of one script inside the Dotfiles Repo, with no arguments or spaces. It runs only after approval on the Machine, tied to the repo and a commit.

safeText.description: Refuses control characters, line separators and invisible or bidi formatting characters, which can make a preview show something other than the file. This also stops Python's $ from accepting a trailing newline, so all three validators agree.

safePathSegments.description: No . or .. segment, no .git segment in any case, and no space at the edge of a segment.

itemId.description: Lowercase kebab-case product name with no category or delivery method in it, such as ghostty or git-identity. It has no dots, so a setting ID fails here.

settingValue.description: A value the Catalog types and checks. There is no null, because leaving the ID out is the only way to say unmanaged, and no nested objects.

settingString.description: Any short printable string. Secret checks are a separate lint stage, not schema rules, so a false positive or a new token prefix can't refuse a whole file.

formulaName.description: A homebrew-core name, or owner/tap/name for a third-party formula. Lowercase, starts with a letter or digit, and has one written form: homebrew/core/x is written x, owner/homebrew-tap/x is written owner/tap/x. Homebrew aliases such as nvim pass here and are resolved from Homebrew's metadata.

caskName.description: A homebrew/cask name, or owner/tap/name for a third-party cask. Same rules as formulaName.

linkTarget.description: Inside the home folder, written with ~/. No absolute paths, no $HOME and no shell metacharacters. Allows non-ASCII letters, parentheses and ~ inside a segment, for real locations such as com~apple~CloudDocs.

repoPath.description: Relative to the Dotfiles Repo root, and can't climb out of it. Same characters as linkTarget. The app also refuses a repo symlink that resolves outside the repo.
